assumptions: One frame, chosen by rule before any matching (earliest sol with a single traverse.json waypoint; middle frame of a 21-frame horizon strip at mastEl ~0.4 deg). Frames tried: 1. Edge-detector settings tried: 1 (sigma 1.5 px, step threshold 4.0 grey levels/px) - no tuning against the match.
Frame is a full-width strip: subframeRect (1,1409,5120,1024) of the 5120x3840 detector, scaleFactor 4, delivered as 1280x256 px. Not the whole 96x73 deg field vertically: only the horizon band.

Optics from the frame's own CAHVORE model (fisheye type, radial terms R, entrance-pupil term E ignored): principal point hc=649, vc=133 in the strip's pixel coordinates, focal ~740 px; field across the strip 96 deg wide. Close to the nominal ~96 deg horizontal Navcam field.

Rover tilt is included via the attitude quaternion in the metadata; camera_vector/mastAz are rover-frame, so true azimuth = rover heading + mastAz (heading from the quaternion, not from mastAz alone as in the original plan).

Quaternion convention is not documented in the API response; two readings tried (boresight azimuth 310 deg vs 125 deg). Reading used: rover_to_site, chosen because its fitted RMS at the waypoint is lower; the other gave fitted RMS 2.67 deg and grid error 2938 m. This 2-way choice was made on the data, so the reported RMS is slightly optimistic.
Position truth = traverse.json waypoint for this sol (sol-level, not the exact imaging position; the rover drove on this sol; accuracy of tens of metres or worse).

Grid search: same 61x61 / 100 m grid and RMS/uncertainty rules as skyline.py, centred on a seeded prior 1-2 km from the waypoint; heading free only within +-10 deg of the nominal azimuth; no elevation offset allowed (a free-offset variant is also reported).

DTM is 20 m CTX; it cannot contain metre-scale rocks and ridges close to the rover, which the camera sees as part of the skyline. Observed skyline can therefore be higher than the DTM horizon in the foreground.

Diagnostic: DTM horizon computed out to 40 km (instead of 15 km) over the same azimuths peaks at -0.05 deg, while the traced skyline is +0.19 to +2.51 deg - the terrain forming the skyline in this frame is not inside the DTM (the DTM covers roughly 30 x 30 km and this waypoint is ~15 km from its eastern edge), so a match is not possible by construction at this heading.
Skyline = first strong bright-to-dark step from the top; columns without an edge or deviating >12 px from a running median are dropped; 5-px median smoothing; resampled onto the 2 deg azimuth grid.
method: Real Navcam frame (NASA/JPL-Caltech raw image), skyline traced and matched against the CTX DTM horizon; single image, hand-tuned edge detection; not simulated.
verdict: POOR match: at the waypoint the traced skyline differs from the DTM horizon by 0.57 deg RMS after fitting a +1.80 deg elevation offset and -2.00 deg azimuth shift (1.90 deg with no fitting). Grid search with the heading limited to +-10 deg lands 2951 m from the waypoint (uncertainty radius 2474 m); with a free elevation offset 4745 m / 1664 m. Diagnostic: DTM horizon computed out to 40 km (instead of 15 km) over the same azimuths peaks at -0.05 deg, while the traced skyline is +0.19 to +2.51 deg - the terrain forming the skyline in this frame is not inside the DTM (the DTM covers roughly 30 x 30 km and this waypoint is ~15 km from its eastern edge), so a match is not possible by construction at this heading. This single real frame does NOT support the claim that a position fix of tens of metres is achievable from one photo with this DTM. Not a statistical result.
